To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
c-erbB2 protein and EGFr are expressed in the epithelium of ovarian inclusion cysts, in benign ovarian tumours, in borderline malignant ovarian tumour, and in a subset of malignant ovarian tumours.
The c-erb-B2 protein is a membrane growth factor receptor with molecular homology to the epidermal growht factor receptor (EGF).
the expression of c-erb B-2 protein is increased and that of the epidermal-growth-factor receptor is reduced in the surface epithelium of ovarian inclusion cysts and in benign ovarian tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of c-erb-B-2 protein and the EGFR in normal ovarian epithelium, in surface inclusion cysts and in common epithelial ovarian tumours.
the immunohistochemistry of c-erb-B-2 protein and the epidermal-growth-factor receptor in ovarian tumours and their precursors.

the immunohistochemistry of the two growth factor receptors, c-erbB2 (HER2/neu) and EGFR, in ovarian epithelial tumours, including normal epithelium, inclusion cysts, benign tumours, borderline tumours, and carcinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-erbB2 protein is a marker of epithelial ovarian cancer and that EGFR expression is related to differentiation and/or clinical stage of ovarian carcinoma.
c-erbB2 protein is expressed in benign and malignant epithelial tumours and that EGFR is absent or expressed weakly in benign tumours but is expressed in malignant tumours.
the expression of both c- erbB-2 protein (HER-2) and EGFR is a common feature in epithelial ovarian tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the c-erbB2 protein and EGPR are not expressed in benign and borderline malignant ovarian tumour, but are expressed in malignant ovarian tumour.
c-erbB2 expression is a useful marker for the diagnosis of benign ovarian tumours.
the expression of EGFR is decreased in the early stage, and that of c-erb-B2 protein is increased in the early stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c-erbB2/EGFR expression pattern may be useful for the diagnosis of ovarian cancer.
EGFR expression is not a reliable marker of EGFR pathway activation in ovarian carcinoma, and the expression of c-erb B-2 protein is increased in the early stage ovarian oncogenesis.
EGFR expression is lost in the early stage ovarian tumorigenesis and that EGFR expression in ovarian cancer may have prognostic value.
